We have applied template 827966 which seems to give a precursor: "Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1". Wait that's same as target but with maybe different substitution? Actually target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. The precursor returned: Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1. That's same but maybe missing the methyl? Actually both have methyl on phenyl? The target has a methyl on first phenyl (para). The precursor also has methyl? "Cc1ccccc1" includes methyl attached to phenyl (toluene). So same. So template didn't break anything? It seems the template is identity? Might be not helpful.

We need retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price < $9999.

We need to design route manually: The target is a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, one with methyl, the other attached to an α,β-unsaturated amide (C= C - C(=O)N- phenyl amine). So we can think disconnections:

1) Break sulfonamide bond: sulfonyl chloride + aniline. So precursor: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and the other aryl amine (the second phenyl with the side chain). The second aryl amine is an aniline bearing the side chain: maybe 4-(E)-3-(phenylamido)acryloyl aniline? Actually the second phenyl is attached to sulfonyl via N (sulfonamide). So we need the aniline: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (no sulfonyl). That's a phenyl with para substituent of the unsaturated amide side chain. So we can get that via amide formation between acryloyl chloride and aniline (3-aminophenyl?). Wait the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N- phenyl-NH2? Actually the side chain is C= C - C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. So it's an amide linking to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the side chain is derived from cinnamoyl chloride reacting with 4-aminophenyl? Actually the amide is between the acryloyl (trans-CH=CH-CO-) and an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we need 4-aminophenyl (aniline) as nucleophile to form amide with acryloyl chloride (or acryloyl bromide). So the phenyl with side chain is 4-(E)-cinnamoyl anilide? Actually the product is phenyl attached to amide nitrogen, and the carbonyl attached to the trans-CH=CH- group. So we can get that by reacting acryloyl chloride with 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl). So the precursor is p-aminophenyl (aniline) with the acryloyl group attached: 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline (i.e., 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline). That is commercially available maybe.

Thus route:

Step 1: Form sulfonamide: React p-toluenesulfonyl chloride with 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline (the aniline). Gives target.

Step 2: Synthesize 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline: Amide formation between acryloyl chloride and p-aminophenyl (4-aminophenyl). Actually acryloyl chloride is CH2=CH-COCl. Reaction with p-aminophenyl gives the amide.

Step 3: p-aminophenyl is commercially available (p-phenylenediamine? Actually p-aminophenyl is aniline with para amino? Wait we need aniline with para position free? The phenyl that will later be sulfonylated is the one with methyl (p-tolyl). The other phenyl is the one bearing the amide side chain; its amine is used for amide formation, then later sulfonylated? Actually the sulfonamide attaches to the nitrogen of that phenyl? Wait the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) via N linking to sulfonyl group, and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) as N-sulfonyl? Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the N is attached to the tolyl ring (aniline) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the tolyl aniline. So we need p-toluidine (p-methylaniline) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So alternative: Use p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (the second phenyl sulfonyl chloride). That may be more feasible: The second phenyl sulfonyl chloride is derived from the phenyl bearing the side chain (the unsaturated amide). So we need to prepare that aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus route:

Step A: Prepare aryl sulfonyl chloride: Starting from 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline (the phenyl with side chain and an NH2). Convert the aniline to sulfonyl chloride? Actually need sulfonyl chloride on that phenyl, not on nitrogen. The sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via S(=O)2 attached to the phenyl carbon (aryl sulfonyl). So we need to sulfonate the phenyl ring to get aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). Typically aryl sulfonyl chlorides are made from sulfonation of benzene (SO3) then chlorination. But maybe commercially available: 4-(E)-cinnamoyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Might be not.

Alternative simpler: Use p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and react with the aniline of the second phenyl (which has the side chain). That gives sulfonamide linking p-tolyl sulfonyl to the second phenyl's amine. That matches target: The sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl (aryl sulfonyl) and nitrogen attached to p-tolyl. Indeed target: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonyl is attached to second phenyl (c2ccc...). The nitrogen attached to p-tolyl. So we need p-toluenesulfonyl chloride + the aniline (second phenyl) which is 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline (has NH2). So step 1: sulfonamide formation.

Thus we need precursor: 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline (commercial?). Likely available. If not, we can synthesize via amide formation from acryloyl chloride + p-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl). That's step 2.

Thus total steps: 2 steps.

Now need to verify commercial availability and price < $9999. Likely both p-toluenesulfonyl chloride and 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline are buyable. If not, we can use p-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine?) Actually p-aminophenyl is just aniline with para amino? That's p-phenylenediamine (has two amines). But we need aniline with para position free (just aniline). The aniline needed is 4-aminophenyl? Wait the phenyl that will have side chain is unsubstituted phenyl (no other substituents) except the amide side chain at para? Actually the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. This phenyl has the side chain at para position (attached via carbon). The amide nitrogen attaches to another phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which is an aniline (has NH2). So the side chain is an amide linking to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the phenyl with side chain is not an aniline; the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl with an NH2 (aniline). So the second phenyl (c3ccccc3N) is an aniline. So the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl bearing the side chain (c2...). That phenyl does not have an NH2. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl, not to the aniline. So the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl bearing side chain (c2...). So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride of that phenyl. That's not commercially available likely.

Thus alternative route: Use p-toluenesulfonyl chloride + aniline (p-aminophenyl) to give sulfonamide linking p-tolyl to aniline. Then later do a Suzuki coupling to attach the side chain? Might be more steps.

Given limited steps, perhaps we can propose a route using commercially available sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and commercially available 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline (which already has the side chain). That yields target directly in one step. So route: single step.

Check if 4-(E)-cinnamoyl aniline is buyable. Let's check via is_buyable.
